story.title: Survivors Rescued After Brooklyn Building Collapse Leaves Two Dead
story.summary: A partial collapse of a three-storey building in Brooklyn resulted in at least two fatalities and 17 injuries. The incident occurred shortly after 4 PM on November 11, with rescuers successfully pulling four survivors from the rubble. Firefighters are continuing their search for additional individuals who may be trapped beneath the debris.

explore_lenses.label: Why does this affect more than the collapse site?
explore_lenses.title: Homes, businesses and a busy corridor were disrupted
explore_lenses.summary: The collapse involved an occupied mixed-use building and damaged a neighboring structure, making this both a rescue emergency and a displacement and neighborhood-access issue.

claims.text: The collapsed building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue had commercial space on the ground floor and four residential units above it, according to building records reviewed by the Associated Press.

The collapse also tore away part of the adjacent building at 1323 Flatbush Avenue, exposing interior rooms; the Red Cross registered 11 adults and two children from six households for emergency assistance.
City officials closed Flatbush Avenue from Clarendon Road to Bedford Avenue and opened a reception center for affected residents at the Flatbush YMCA.

City officials closed Flatbush Avenue from Clarendon Road to Bedford Avenue and opened a reception center for affected residents at the Flatbush YMCA.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The full extent and duration of displacement, neighboring-building damage and street closures had not been determined in the city’s November 11 briefing.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about the adjacent construction?
explore_lenses.title: Excavation was underway under approved plans
explore_lenses.summary: Officials have identified excavation at the neighboring development site as the work underway when the building fell, but have not concluded that it caused the collapse or that any permit requirement was violated.

claims.text: Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani said workers were excavating at the adjacent site when the collapse occurred; he said the site had approval for a three-story building, while a separate nine-story proposal had not been approved.

Filed support-of-excavation plans for 2625 Bedford Avenue identify 1321 Flatbush Avenue as an adjacent building and require work to conform to the building code, project safety documents and field-condition verification requirements.

Records reviewed by Engineering News-Record show DOB issued earthwork and support-of-excavation permits on September 9, with excavation authorized to reach 14 feet below grade and special inspection required for sheeting, shoring and bracing.
The Department of Buildings says the cause remains under investigation; the existence of excavation and permits does not establish causation or responsibility.

explore_lenses.label: What happens before investigators can answer why?
explore_lenses.title: Rescue crews must complete a hazardous search
explore_lenses.summary: The immediate priority is a methodical search of unstable debris and remaining void spaces; only then can the site be fully examined for the cause and for potential code or enforcement issues.

claims.text: FDNY Chief John Esposito said crews were using FDNY and NYPD dogs to identify void spaces, then planned selective debris removal down to the ground to search for additional victims.
Esposito said the operation faced a risk of secondary collapse from the adjoining partially intact building, requiring careful, choreographed debris movement.
Forecast: Esposito said FDNY would likely remain at the site for several days until the entire area had been searched for potential victims.
The mayor said DOB and law-enforcement partners would lead the cause investigation after the emergency response, while DOB inspectors assessed nearby structural stability.

story_report.summary: A partial collapse of a three-storey building in Brooklyn killed at least two people and injured 17 others. Four survivors were pulled from the rubble as emergency crews continued searching the debris, where officials said additional victims could still be found. The response also extended beyond the collapsed structure, with nearby buildings assessed for stability and assistance opened for displaced residents.

sections.heading: Residents Face Damage and Displacement
sections.body: Building records reviewed by the Associated Press describe 1321 Flatbush Avenue as having commercial space at street level and four residential units above. The collapse tore away part of the neighboring building at 1323 Flatbush Avenue, exposing interior rooms, ABC7 reported. The Red Cross registered 11 adults and two children from six households for emergency assistance, while the city closed Flatbush Avenue between Clarendon Road and Bedford Avenue and opened a reception center at the Flatbush YMCA.

sections.heading: Excavation Work Draws Official Scrutiny
sections.body: Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani said workers were excavating at an adjacent site when the building collapsed. Filed support-of-excavation plans for 2625 Bedford Avenue identify 1321 Flatbush Avenue as an adjacent building and require compliance with building-code, safety-document and field-condition requirements. Records reviewed by Engineering News-Record indicate earthwork and support-of-excavation permits were issued Sept. 9, authorizing excavation up to 14 feet below grade and requiring special inspection of sheeting, shoring and bracing.

sections.heading: Rescue Teams Search Unstable Debris
sections.body: FDNY Chief John Esposito said crews were using FDNY and NYPD dogs to locate void spaces before selectively removing debris down to ground level. He said the adjoining partially intact building created a risk of secondary collapse, requiring carefully coordinated debris movement. Esposito said FDNY would likely remain for several days, while the Department of Buildings and law-enforcement partners prepare to lead the cause investigation after the emergency response.

unresolved.text: Investigators had not publicly identified a mechanical or structural cause of the collapse or assigned responsibility as of Nov. 12.
Officials did not know how many people, if any, remained unaccounted for, and no timetable for investigative findings had been announced.
The full extent and duration of displacement, neighboring-building damage and the street closure had not been determined in the city’s Nov. 11 briefing.

related_stories.title: Two Iranian Men Convicted in UK for Spying on Journalists
related_stories.summary: A London court has convicted two Iranian citizens of spying on journalists associated with a Persian-language television station critical of the Iranian government. The court found that the men were promised rewards for sending intelligence back to Iran, and one of them was also convicted of planning a violent attack against the journalists.

related_stories.title: Tragic Building Collapse in Brooklyn Claims Eight Lives, Including Two Children
related_stories.summary: A building collapse in the Flatbush area of Brooklyn has resulted in the deaths of eight individuals, including two children. The incident occurred when a three-story apartment building fell into a neighboring construction site. Rescue operations are ongoing, with hundreds of firefighters involved in the search for potential survivors.
